Càite bheil a h-uile sìon air a dhol? Abney has so many precious things he decides to put on a display, which gets longer and longer until... uh oh, where has everything gone?

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha caraidean Pheicein ag innse dha mun t-sanas ùr aig “Silidh Milis Steigeach”, ma ghlèidheas tu ochd bileagan bho na mullaich, gheibh thu paidhir spèileachain. ’S e an trioblaid, gu bheil blas grot far “Silidh Milis Steigeach”. Petit finds out if you collect eight Really Tasty Candy lids you get a free pair of roller skates! The only catch is Really Tasty Candy tastes really, really, bad...

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Abigail NicÌomhair a’ leughadh Dè bhios Dadaidh a’ dèanamh? Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh is a dhealbhachadh le Rachel Bright, agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. Abigail MacIver reads Dè bhios Dadaidh a’ dèanamh? It was written and illustrated by Rachel Bright and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Saoil a bheil 'n Orca Dhorch fo smachd thaibhsean? Chan eil sgeul air duine – càite bheil iad uile? Is the Dark Orca under the influence of ghosts? There’s no sign of anyone. Where are they all?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha Tbh ùr aig an tuathanach is abair gu bheil e toilichte. The farmer is very excited about his new TV.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha na Pluic an dùil a dhol sìos chun na tràghad airson co-là-breith Anna, ach nuair a tha biadh partaidh Phòil gan dèanamh beag bìodach, feumaidh iad dòigh eile a lorg airson faighinn ann. The Spuds have planned a trip to the seaside for Anna’s birthday, but when Dave’s party food shrinks them, they must adapt and find a way for the outing to still go ahead.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Granaidh air a bualadh le dealanach, is tha seo ga fàgail làn dealain. Feumaidh Pòl feuchainn ris an dealain aice a dhrùdhadh aiste coltach ri bataraidh, mus dèan i cus cron. When Gran gets struck by lightning and charged with electrical powers, Dave must run her down like a battery before she causes too much mischief.

programme.title: Dùbhlain DIY (Instructions Not Included)
programme.desc: Derek 'Pluto' Murray hosts a fun knockout amateur DIY competition where couples go head to head. Derek 'Pluto' Moireach le farpais spòrsail DIY is cupail a’ strì an aghaidh a chèile.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Political Journalist Niall O’Gallagher is Joy’s studio guest, and Calum Maclean visits a location in Islay which is both historic and political.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Dealbhan Fraoich/Heather's Portraits
programme.desc: Heather Dewar visits Skye where she draws a colour portrait of Neil MacKinnon. Fraoch Nic an Deòir san Eilean Sgitheanach a’dèanamh dealbh dathte de Niall MacFhionghain.

programme.title: Luchd-Brathaidh Cogaidh | Spies of War
programme.desc: An Lùnastal 1949: ceithir bliadhna an dèidh do na Stàitean Aonaichte boma niùclasach a chleachdadh, tha an t-Aonadh Sobhietach air am boma aca fhèin a chruthachadh. Cha robh dùil ri seo cho luath. Air cùl ghnothaichean, tha lìonra farsaing de luch-brathaidh air fiosrachadh dìomhair a lìbhrigeadh gu na Sobhietaich. Ionnsaich mar a thug luchd-saidheans seachad fiosrachadh mun bhoma – agus mar a chaidh an còd aca a bhriseadh. In August 1949, four years after the US drops the atomic bomb, the Soviets detonate one. No-one expected it so soon. Behind the scenes, a vast Soviet spy network helps deliver the secret. Discover how scientists passed on the bomb’s secrets, and how their code was broken. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc: Skipinnish le Land Below the Waves ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann. Skipinnish perform Land Below the Waves in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: Glan Fhèin
programme.desc: Angela clashes with angry locals shouting about short-term lets. Betty and Dido de-escalate things and share some home truths. There’s a sticky situation when an activist called Adam sneaks through the catflap with a tube of superglue. Meanwhile, Daniel tests Katie’s management methods by renegotiating his contract. And a corporate relaunch that is definitely not a party features costumes, cocktails, new clients and wild dance moves. Ultimately the rivals seem to be getting closer than ever.

programme.title: Murchadh MacPhàrlain: Bard Mhealboist
programme.desc: Tha na facail aig Murachadh MacPharlain rin cluinntinn air bilean ginealach as deidh ginealach , rud a tha fios a bheireadh toileachas dhan duine uasal seo a bha cho ladair na sheasamh a thaobh canan agus cultar nan Gaidheal. B'e techneolas gu ire mhor a dh'fhag gun thachair sin agus an inneal-claraidh a' fagail gum b'urrain na facail agus na fuinn aige a' sgaoileadh na b' fharsainge. Tha am program seo a'deanamh dealbh air an duine agus a bhuaidh a th'aige fhathast air beatha nan Gaidheal. Award-winning documentary profiling Murdo MacFarlane, the Melbost Bard and renowned Gaelic poet and songwriter from the island of Lewis, whose work was a catalyst for a whole new era of modern Gaelic music. Having composed poems and songs all his life, it was not until the advent of the tape recorder that Murdo, who could neither read nor write music, became known to a wider audience. Featuring TV and radio archive recordings of Murdo being interviewed and performances of his work.

programme.title: Transatlantic Sessions
programme.desc: Sreath ùr. Julie Fowlis le taghadh ciùil bho dà dheichead de Transatlantic Sessions. Julie Fowlis presents highlights from two decades of Transatlantic Sessions.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take you so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. Three senior managers from a national bookstore face off against a team drawn together by their love of London's retro bowling alleys. Who will win the battle as they compete to draw together the connections between things, which, at first glance, seem utterly random?

programme.title: Universe
programme.desc: A space mission discovers the dramatic history of the Milky Way. Professor Brian Cox reveals how our galaxy endured multiple collisions as rival galaxies fought for survival.

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: The second round of quarter-finals concludes with an elimination match. Two teams return having lost their first quarter-finals; a second loss here means they leave the competition. Jeremy Paxman asks the questions.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take you so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. In the first of the quarter-finals, three fans of the Archers radio series take on the combined knowledge of three flatmates who all met up at Exeter University. They compete to draw together the connections between things, which, at first glance, seem utterly random - from Castor and Pollux to Brahma to Yoshi to Orville the Duck.

programme.title: Double Cross: The True Story of the D-Day Spies
programme.desc: The story of D-Day has been told from the point of view of the soldiers who fought in it, the tacticians who planned it and the generals who led it. But that epic event in world history has never been told before through the perspective of the strange handful of spies who made it possible. D-Day was a great victory of arms, a tactical coup, and a moral crusade. But it was also a triumph for espionage, deceit, and thinking of the most twisted sort. Following on from his hugely successful BBC Two documentaries, Operation Mincemeat and Double Agent: The Eddie Chapman Story (Agent Zigzag), writer and presenter Ben Macintyre returns to the small screen to bring to life his third best-selling book - Double Cross The True Story of the D-Day Spies. Macintyre reveals the gripping true story of five of the double agents who helped to make D-Day such a success.

programme.title: This World
programme.desc: Simon Reeve heads to Vietnam to uncover the stories behind the morning pick-me-up. He travels to the central highlands, where he meets the people who grow, pick and pack coffee.

programme.title: The Producers
programme.desc: A struggling producer and timid accountant scheme to make money by putting on a Broadway show they know will flop, so none of the numerous investors will expect their cash back. A tasteless glorification of Hitler and the Nazis looks guaranteed to fail.

programme.title: Mel Brooks and Me - by Alan Yentob
programme.desc: Alan Yentob looks back on his experiences working with the great Mel Brooks, who was awarded an Honorary Oscar in 2024 in recognition of a boundary-breaking career that shocked audiences but always left them laughing too. Alan reflects on what it was like being a producer encountering the comic genius who created The Producers and how his and Mel’s working relationship quickly developed into something that one newspaper critic once described as nothing less than a love story.

programme.title: imagine...
programme.desc: At the age of 91, Mel Brooks is unstoppable, with his musical Young Frankenstein opening to great critical acclaim in London in late 2017. Alan Yentob visits Mel at home in Hollywood, at work and at play. With the aid of BBC archive stretching back decades, together they embark on an unpredictable, irresistible journey through the city of stars, meeting the legendary Carl Reiner along the way. The driver is Mel Brooks - you have been warned!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: As the red and blue teams weave their way around an antiques arcade in Hungerford, Caroline Hawley tries her hand at weaving willow. In the workshop of Erica Adams, she learns about the history of wicker and its resurgence as a sustainable material for making baskets and furniture. On the red team, couple Jonjo and Scarlett are aiming to 'write themselves into Bargain Hunt history', with some expert help from Raj Bisram. The art deco fans soon spot a stylish period coffee set, but will they decide to splash out? Over with the blue team, Stephanie Connell is the guide for husband-and-wife duo Liz and Ian. Liz wants to buy something 'quirky, different and unique', while Ian wants to go 'big and bold'. Animal-related antiques seem to be the order or the day - but will an owl money box or a ceramic cobra win them over? Down the road in Newbury, auctioneer Thomas Forrester puts the teams’ items under the gavel, but which team will come out on top?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A stop-and-search uncovers cannabis, CCTV supports a mall assault inquiry, and officers track risky teen riders as a long-serving officer ends her shift with major career news.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A scammer posing as a broadband internet provider tries to steal money from a man by remotely accessing his device – but the team in the scam hub have other ideas. Repeated efforts to get through to the target by Rav and Nick fail, leading to a race against time as ground interceptor Nathan hits the road to try and prevent the scam in person. With serious cash on the line and a highly persistent scammer, there are no guarantees, and Rav finds himself in a tit-for-tat with the man unsure who to believe.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sun, sea and seals... it’s another glorious escape to the country in Cornwall, where Alistair Appleton is helping a retired couple from the Wirral find their perfect Cornish retreat within walking distance of a pub. After years of happy family holidays there, and now with their son and new grandson living locally, they’re ready to make the move and live in Cornwall full-time. With a £400,000 budget and a love of bungalows, the couple are given some tempting options by Alistair. He also pops by the Cornish Seal Sanctuary to meet some of its permanent and temporary residents.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee Burkhill and Chris Hull are in Tamworth to transform mum Jade and daughter Charlie’s tiny, unloved plot into a pink-inspired garden. They both love all shades of the colour, from magenta to mauve, and feel this would be a perfect palette for their forever home. Can the team achieve all this on a £4,500 budget?

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Izzie and JJ help Michael and Clara clear their busy home and revive forgotten gems to sell at auction, but will they raise enough to give Michael’s parents a day out to remember?

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Lucy Porter. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: The One Show

programme.title: EastEnders

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon is back in the host’s chair for the award-winning comedy panel show, with Lee Mack and David Mitchell returning as team captains. Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting fact from fiction this week are guests Raj Bisram, Deborah Frances-White, Stephen Mulhern and Jenny Ryan.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as Ecuador play Germany in their final Group E match at the New Jersey Stadium in New York. Four-time winners Germany have uncharacteristically struggled at the past two World Cups, going out in the group stage on both occasions. Ecuador proved incredibly hard to beat in South American qualifying, conceding just five times in 18 matches as they finished second behind Argentina and ahead of the likes of Brazil and Colombia. These two teams have met once before at a World Cup, with Germany winning 3-0 in the group stage of the 2006 tournament.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the final match in Group F in Dallas between two former World Cup hosts, Japan and Sweden. Sweden reached the quarter-finals in their last World Cup appearance in 2018, where they were beaten by England. Japan are at their seventh consecutive finals but have never previously made it past the first knockout round.

Repeated efforts to get through to the target by Rav and Nick fail, leading to a race against time as ground interceptor Nathan hits the road to try and prevent the scam in person. With serious cash on the line and a highly persistent scammer, there are no guarantees, and Rav finds himself in a tit-for-tat with the man unsure who to believe.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sun, sea and seals... it’s another glorious escape to the country in Cornwall, where Alistair Appleton is helping a retired couple from the Wirral find their perfect Cornish retreat within walking distance of a pub. After years of happy family holidays there, and now with their son and new grandson living locally, they’re ready to make the move and live in Cornwall full-time. With a £400,000 budget and a love of bungalows, the couple are given some tempting options by Alistair. He also pops by the Cornish Seal Sanctuary to meet some of its permanent and temporary residents.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee Burkhill and Chris Hull are in Tamworth to transform mum Jade and daughter Charlie’s tiny, unloved plot into a pink-inspired garden. They both love all shades of the colour, from magenta to mauve, and feel this would be a perfect palette for their forever home. Can the team achieve all this on a £4,500 budget?

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Izzie and JJ help Michael and Clara clear their busy home and revive forgotten gems to sell at auction, but will they raise enough to give Michael’s parents a day out to remember?

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon is back in the host’s chair for the award-winning comedy panel show, with Lee Mack and David Mitchell returning as team captains. Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting fact from fiction this week are guests Raj Bisram, Deborah Frances-White, Stephen Mulhern and Jenny Ryan.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as Ecuador play Germany in their final Group E match at the New Jersey Stadium in New York. Four-time winners Germany have uncharacteristically struggled at the past two World Cups, going out in the group stage on both occasions. Ecuador proved incredibly hard to beat in South American qualifying, conceding just five times in 18 matches as they finished second behind Argentina and ahead of the likes of Brazil and Colombia. These two teams have met once before at a World Cup, with Germany winning 3-0 in the group stage of the 2006 tournament.

programme.title: BBC News at Ten
programme.desc: The latest national and international news, with reports from BBC correspondents worldwide.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the final match in Group F in Dallas between two former World Cup hosts, Japan and Sweden. Sweden reached the quarter-finals in their last World Cup appearance in 2018, where they were beaten by England. Japan are at their seventh consecutive finals but have never previously made it past the first knockout round.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the final game in Group A, where Czech Republic take on hosts Mexico in Mexico City. Czech Republic last qualified for the World Cup finals 20 years ago, when they exited at the group stage. Mexico were also eliminated at the first hurdle four years ago in Qatar and will be hoping that home support can improve their fortunes this time around. Czech Republic won the only previous match between the two countries, a friendly in Hong Kong in 2000.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: As the red and blue teams weave their way around an antiques arcade in Hungerford, Caroline Hawley tries her hand at weaving willow. In the workshop of Erica Adams, she learns about the history of wicker and its resurgence as a sustainable material for making baskets and furniture. On the red team, couple Jonjo and Scarlett are aiming to 'write themselves into Bargain Hunt history', with some expert help from Raj Bisram. The art deco fans soon spot a stylish period coffee set, but will they decide to splash out? Over with the blue team, Stephanie Connell is the guide for husband-and-wife duo Liz and Ian. Liz wants to buy something 'quirky, different and unique', while Ian wants to go 'big and bold'. Animal-related antiques seem to be the order or the day - but will an owl money box or a ceramic cobra win them over? Down the road in Newbury, auctioneer Thomas Forrester puts the teams’ items under the gavel, but which team will come out on top?

programme.desc: As the red and blue teams weave their way around an antiques arcade in Hungerford, Caroline Hawley tries her hand at weaving willow. In the workshop of Erica Adams, she learns about the history of wicker and its resurgence as a sustainable material for making baskets and furniture. On the red team, couple Jonjo and Scarlett are aiming to 'write themselves into Bargain Hunt history', with some expert help from Raj Bisram. The art deco fans soon spot a stylish period coffee set, but will they decide to splash out? Over with the blue team, Stephanie Connell is the guide for husband-and-wife duo Liz and Ian. Liz wants to buy something 'quirky, different and unique', while Ian wants to go 'big and bold'. Animal-related antiques seem to be the order or the day - but will an owl money box or a ceramic cobra win them over? Down the road in Newbury, auctioneer Thomas Forrester puts the teams’ items under the gavel, but which team will come out on top?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: As the red and blue teams weave their way around an antiques arcade in Hungerford, Caroline Hawley tries her hand at weaving willow. In the workshop of Erica Adams, she learns about the history of wicker and its resurgence as a sustainable material for making baskets and furniture. On the red team, couple Jonjo and Scarlett are aiming to 'write themselves into Bargain Hunt history', with some expert help from Raj Bisram. The art deco fans soon spot a stylish period coffee set, but will they decide to splash out? Over with the blue team, Stephanie Connell is the guide for husband-and-wife duo Liz and Ian. Liz wants to buy something 'quirky, different and unique', while Ian wants to go 'big and bold'. Animal-related antiques seem to be the order or the day - but will an owl money box or a ceramic cobra win them over? Down the road in Newbury, auctioneer Thomas Forrester puts the teams’ items under the gavel, but which team will come out on top?

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A stop-and-search uncovers cannabis, CCTV supports a mall assault inquiry, and officers track risky teen riders as a long-serving officer ends her shift with major career news.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A scammer posing as a broadband internet provider tries to steal money from a man by remotely accessing his device – but the team in the scam hub have other ideas. Repeated efforts to get through to the target by Rav and Nick fail, leading to a race against time as ground interceptor Nathan hits the road to try and prevent the scam in person. With serious cash on the line and a highly persistent scammer, there are no guarantees, and Rav finds himself in a tit-for-tat with the man unsure who to believe.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sun, sea and seals... it’s another glorious escape to the country in Cornwall, where Alistair Appleton is helping a retired couple from the Wirral find their perfect Cornish retreat within walking distance of a pub. After years of happy family holidays there, and now with their son and new grandson living locally, they’re ready to make the move and live in Cornwall full-time. With a £400,000 budget and a love of bungalows, the couple are given some tempting options by Alistair. He also pops by the Cornish Seal Sanctuary to meet some of its permanent and temporary residents.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee Burkhill and Chris Hull are in Tamworth to transform mum Jade and daughter Charlie’s tiny, unloved plot into a pink-inspired garden. programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon is back in the host’s chair for the award-winning comedy panel show, with Lee Mack and David Mitchell returning as team captains. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as Ecuador play Germany in their final Group E match at the New Jersey Stadium in New York. Four-time winners Germany have uncharacteristically struggled at the past two World Cups, going out in the group stage on both occasions. Ecuador proved incredibly hard to beat in South American qualifying, conceding just five times in 18 matches as they finished second behind Argentina and ahead of the likes of Brazil and Colombia. These two teams have met once before at a World Cup, with Germany winning 3-0 in the group stage of the 2006 tournament.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the final match in Group F in Dallas between two former World Cup hosts, Japan and Sweden. Sweden reached the quarter-finals in their last World Cup appearance in 2018, where they were beaten by England. Japan are at their seventh consecutive finals but have never previously made it past the first knockout round.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the final game in Group A, where Czech Republic take on hosts Mexico in Mexico City. Czech Republic last qualified for the World Cup finals 20 years ago, when they exited at the group stage. Mexico were also eliminated at the first hurdle four years ago in Qatar and will be hoping that home support can improve their fortunes this time around. Czech Republic won the only previous match between the two countries, a friendly in Hong Kong in 2000.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: As the red and blue teams weave their way around an antiques arcade in Hungerford, Caroline Hawley tries her hand at weaving willow. In the workshop of Erica Adams, she learns about the history of wicker and its resurgence as a sustainable material for making baskets and furniture. On the red team, couple Jonjo and Scarlett are aiming to 'write themselves into Bargain Hunt history', with some expert help from Raj Bisram. The art deco fans soon spot a stylish period coffee set, but will they decide to splash out? Over with the blue team, Stephanie Connell is the guide for husband-and-wife duo Liz and Ian. Liz wants to buy something 'quirky, different and unique', while Ian wants to go 'big and bold'. Animal-related antiques seem to be the order or the day - but will an owl money box or a ceramic cobra win them over? Down the road in Newbury, auctioneer Thomas Forrester puts the teams’ items under the gavel, but which team will come out on top?

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A stop-and-search uncovers cannabis, CCTV supports a mall assault inquiry, and officers track risky teen riders as a long-serving officer ends her shift with major career news.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A scammer posing as a broadband internet provider tries to steal money from a man by remotely accessing his device – but the team in the scam hub have other ideas. Repeated efforts to get through to the target by Rav and Nick fail, leading to a race against time as ground interceptor Nathan hits the road to try and prevent the scam in person. With serious cash on the line and a highly persistent scammer, there are no guarantees, and Rav finds himself in a tit-for-tat with the man unsure who to believe.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sun, sea and seals... it’s another glorious escape to the country in Cornwall, where Alistair Appleton is helping a retired couple from the Wirral find their perfect Cornish retreat within walking distance of a pub. After years of happy family holidays there, and now with their son and new grandson living locally, they’re ready to make the move and live in Cornwall full-time. With a £400,000 budget and a love of bungalows, the couple are given some tempting options by Alistair. He also pops by the Cornish Seal Sanctuary to meet some of its permanent and temporary residents.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee Burkhill and Chris Hull are in Tamworth to transform mum Jade and daughter Charlie’s tiny, unloved plot into a pink-inspired garden. They both love all shades of the colour, from magenta to mauve, and feel this would be a perfect palette for their forever home. Can the team achieve all this on a £4,500 budget?

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: Paul discovers the source of the remarkable River Nith, high in a remote forestry plantation. Heading downstream, he hears the story of the Knockshinnoch mining disaster – how 116 men were saved from entombment after a massive earth collapse. At Sanquhar, once famous for its unique and distinctive knitting pattern, Paul tries very hard to knit a glove before it all unravels. Kirkpatrick Macmillan was the man first credited with making a bicycle with pedals. Paul wobbles in his wake aboard a replica at Drumlanrig Castle, before heading south to Ellisland – once the riverside home of the poet Robert Burns. In Dumfries, Paul learns how astronaut Neil Armstrong might not have walked on the surface of the moon without the optical skills of a local man. Journey’s end is at Caerlaverock Castle overlooking the shining sands of the Solway Firth.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Kirsty plants meconopsis, and Brian is in the 6x8 greenhouse looking at what you can do if you have this standard-sized glasshouse. Also, a visit to a great community garden in the Easterhouse area of Glasgow that is used and enjoyed by a range of groups in the local community, and handy hints. Kirsty and Brian start a new feature that gives 'everything you need to know' plant profiles on some of the country’s most popular garden varieties - from growing patterns and soil preference to pruning plans. Throughout the series are fact files on some of the plants most often found in viewers' plots.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: The last programme of the spring series, Dougie and the team are at Ingliston for The Royal Highland Show. Cammy catches up with a professional sheep dresser as he makes finishing touches before showing his Bleu du Maines. As Landward celebrates fifty years on air, Dougie looks back on show coverage from the archive. Rosie gets a taste of Aberdeenshire in the food and drink hall showcasing artisan producers, Arlene visits the honey tent to find about the complexities of judging the amber nectar, Cammy’s hoping to win a red rosette in the show ring with his Jersey dairy cow. And Dougie steps into the main ring to follow the spectacular grand parade.

programme.title: Inside Barlinnie
programme.desc: After 18 months behind bars, Sean returns to his community in Cambuslang, where he struggles to manage his ADHD, battles with addiction and faces a court case for armed robbery. Self-styled vigilante Frankie lives by his own brutal code of 'jail justice', which sees him attacking sex offenders, while violent offender and drug user Owen attempts to rebuild his life on the outside, until his violent past catches up with him.

programme.title: Only an Excuse
programme.desc: A special selection of sketches picked from 27 years of the hit Scottish comedy. Tackling Scottish football and much more besides, and mixing classic characters, favourite skits and hilarious media spoofs. Discover just why they are bouncing so high in the Celtic dugout and see how the Rangers gaffer chooses his team. Frankie Boy rocks up at the petrol station, King Kenny dispenses managerial advice on the golf course and Sir Fergie lectures on leadership at Harvard. Find out the secrets of a Brechin pie and what the Thunbergs really get up to when Greta is away.

programme.title: Janey and Ashley Get a Real Job
programme.desc: Janey and Ashley don hard hats and head for a construction site. They are set to work making mortar, and they find out just how hard it is to build a simple wall. Next up, they have to get their heads around more complicated tools to connect cold and hot water pipes. Their work is then put to the test when it’s hooked up to the live water main, and it could be a disaster if the site starts filling up with water! However, their biggest challenge comes when they have to insulate a wall. The job involves joinery, accurate measuring and trying not to waste expensive materials. Can Ashley and Janey get past the hilarity of the word ‘dwang’? Can they put in the hard graft to see the shift through? And which one will be named ‘best employee’ and avoid that last awful job?

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Conversation about Scotland’s biggest news stories, hosted by Martin Geissler.

programme.title: Life on the Bay
programme.desc: Owner and manager Alan shows his daughter the ropes as she sees another side to the family business. The Fife caravan park has been operating under restrictions for 18 months, but at last things are starting to return to normal, and staff and caravan residents are desperate to get back to doing the things they love. Former martial arts champion Alan puts on a taekwondo training session, there’s a live music performance for residents and guests, and a caravan owner and music lover hosts a jam session.

programme.title: Top Gear

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Calamity James is a slapstick comedy about a young man, James, who is cursed with ‘acute misfortune syndrome’. In this world, chronic bad luck exists and the unbelievable is the everyday.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Jack is an unfulfilled actor who is desperate for some meaningful work. He agrees to join fellow thespian Lauren on a pantomime tour of the north east. Just one catch: it’s an off-season tour of dementia homes, where the audience tend to be more interested in daytime TV than in Jack and Lauren’s contemporary interpretation of Alice in Wonderland. Lauren remains relentlessly upbeat, but Jack fears he’s sunk to a new low... until he is unexpectedly confronted with the reality of life, his future and where it ends.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Wildlife presenter Steve Backshall is on a quest to meet 60 of the deadliest animals on the planet. Steve and his team are on a fun-filled, adrenalin-fuelled journey to find those animals most people spend their lifetime avoiding. The action kicks off in Hoedspruit, South Africa. The adventure is nearly over before it's even begun as an angry hippo surprises Steve in a tense encounter on the river. Unscathed and undaunted by the first deadly animal on his list, Steve gets up close and personal with some of South Africa's deadliest snakes and spends the night under the stars in order to find a particularly venomous scorpion.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Wildlife presenter Steve Backshall is on a quest to meet 60 of the deadliest animals on the planet. Steve and his team are on a fun-filled, adrenalin-fuelled journey to find those animals most people spend their lifetime avoiding. When a Nile crocodile attacks a local girl in her own swimming pool, Steve decides to investigate these ancient reptiles and to judge for himself whether they deserve their deadly reputation. He pits himself against the mighty fish eagle as he tries his hand at diving for his supper, and takes to the South African skies to try and find one of Africa's most elusive predators, the awesome hunting dog.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May compare the Mercedes SLS, the Porsche 911 GT3 RS and the Ferrari 458 Italia in an epic road trip up America's east coast. Plus a round-up of car-related Christmas stuff and another celebrity takes to the track as the star in a Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: The Traitors US
programme.desc: The latest mission offers the chance to stop the night's murder – but only if the Faithful stick together. After an explosive Round Table, one Traitor is under pressure from an influential player. But can they murder him to stop him talking?

programme.title: The Traitors US
programme.desc: The Faithful plan a coup, and one Traitor is accused to their face. The Round Table brings difficult decisions, and with the temperature in the turret at boiling point, the Traitors must pull off the bloodiest murder this castle has ever seen.

programme.title: OnlyFans: Inside the Machine
programme.desc: Behind the billion-pound success of OnlyFans lies a hidden ecosystem of exploitation. A BBC Current Affairs investigation uncovers allegations of exploitation, coercion and violence committed by some of the hundreds of agents who manage many of the platform’s creators as well as the potential for modern slavery. Through survivor testimony, undercover access to a managers’ chat forum and expert legal analysis, the film exposes an industry where young women are trapped, threatened and profited from - raising urgent questions about accountability at the heart of one of Britain's most lucrative tech companies.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: In southern Africa, a pride of lions has rewritten the rules by learning to take down elephants. In this follow-up to Africa's Giant Killers, we join the pride at the start of the rainy season. As the elephants depart, a catalogue of dramatic events unfolds. The pride males turn against each other, an inexperienced mum puts her newborn cubs in mortal danger, a rival group of lions challenges the pride for its territory and, when lightning strikes, fires burn day and night. When the dust eventually settles, the pride is left with only one choice - to face their old foe, the elephants, or risk starvation. The final showdown awaits.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as South Africa play their final Group A game against South Korea in Monterrey. It's been 24 years since South Korea reached the semi-finals on home soil in 2002. They’ve made it to the round of 16 on two occasions since, including Qatar 2022, where they claimed a dramatic last-gasp win over Portugal in their final group game.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: The competition kicks off in Belfast as Vernon Kay and unreliable tour guide Paul Gorton serve up facts, fibs and playful distractions as the celebrity players attempt to sort truth from twaddle. This week’s guests are presenter Owain Wyn Evans, Olympic champion Greg Rutherford and Blue Peter’s Abby Cook, and their competition kicks off in Belfast. A daily winner is declared at the end of each show, with scores building across the five days as the race to reveal the week's overall champion gets going.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: On patrol in Belfast, Perri and Adam respond to reports of cars performing dangerous stunts on the streets while large crowds look on. When they arrive, the cars scatter and the Peelers don’t catch anyone. Later, they put in place an operation to disrupt a group of so-called differs – drivers who dangerously and illegally spin their cars in circles on main roads. The Peelers call in air support and try to catch a differ in the act. Back in Belfast, the team receive reports of two women being disruptive at a hotel. On arrival, one of the women greets Stephen and it looks like she’ll cooperate with police. But outside, things turn ugly, and after assaulting another woman, she is arrested and brought into custody. It’s not a quiet journey.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Richie Anderson is in rural Lincolnshire, helping John and Margaret find a large countryside home, with enough room for six visiting grandchildren, on a budget of £400,000. They explore wonderful properties, including one with a delightful garden, as well as a mystery house close to the coast. Richie also visits a former 300-acre farm now being transformed through an ambitious rewilding project.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: It's carnival time, one of the biggest celebrations of the summer season in Hamilton. Community Officer PC Chris Douglas is preparing for the island’s annual parade, swapping uniform for a handmade, colourful costume, while his colleagues stay on duty to keep the celebrations running smoothly as thousands line the streets to dance and party. Acting Inspector Tiffany Caisey and Sergeant Mervin Homer move from roadside stops to an unusual call at Dockyard, where a missing phone leads them to a cruise ship packed with 3,000 passengers and the tricky task of locating it on board. In central Hamilton, Sergeant Helen McHugh, K9 handler PC Robin MacNab and her dog Roni head into a park linked to drug activity tracking down a man, who when searched, reveals he’s in possession of a crack pipe and associated drug paraphernalia. Coastguard Corporal Quentin Burgess and Private Matthew Stephens are patrolling the waters, carrying out checks ahead of a busy maritime weekend. In the the run-up to carnival, Officer Chris teams up with PC Krishna Singh and PC Oba Swan to offer crime prevention advice to locals, a reminder of the close community ties that shape island life.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: A special programme from Birmingham in the heart of Gardeners’ World Live – an annual vibrant celebration of practical gardening and bold design. Monty Don is joined by Frances Tophill, Adam Frost, Arit Anderson and Sue Kent for an hour packed with ideas, inspiration and expert advice. The team explore standout gardens, meet the people shaping the future of horticulture and reveal practical takeaways viewers can try at home. Sustainability is in the spotlight as pioneering growers reveal why cork could be a game-changing material – and how it’s already transforming the way they garden. There’s a surprising and ambitious show garden co-designed by Professor Alice Roberts, bringing the story of evolution to life through plants, and a first-time designer whose passion for railways has inspired a unique garden guaranteed to turn heads.

programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The quiz show where players must avoid Impossible answers to stay in the competition. 21 people start today’s show but how many of them will survive to face the £10,000 question?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: In the final heat, four contenders take on the famous black chair, answering questions on their chosen specialist subjects to earn a place in the semi-finals. Clive Myrie hosts, with contenders answering questions on Christiaan Huygens, Jonathan Creek, the life and works of Artemisia Gentileschi, and European mammals.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Chris and Meg's Wild Summer
programme.desc: Chris Packham and stepdaughter Meg McCubbin visit a kittiwake colony, snorkel with grey seals, explore Lindisfarne island and take a boat to Bass Rock, home to 150,000 gannets.

programme.title: Britain and the Sea
programme.desc: This third episode traces the crucial importance of the sea to Britain's trade and to individual livelihoods of coastal communities. Joined on this leg of his epic sail by his son Fred, David follows the trade routes of the west coast of Scotland along the monumental channels that cut through the romantic Highlands and brought wealth and prosperity to the heart of Scotland. The journey starts at Craobh Haven and takes David along the Crinan Canal, around the Isle of Bute and up the River Clyde towards Glasgow.

programme.title: Wild West - America's Great Frontier
programme.desc: From the mysterious Sea of Cortez to the wild and elemental Pacific Ocean, powerful earth forces shape the coastline of the wild west. These restless shores are a magnet for life. They are visited by the greatest of all animals, the blue whale, and by strange fish that come ashore on the full moon to spawn in their thousands. Fog-shrouded headlands nurture massive coastal redwoods, and swollen-nosed lizards eke out a living on remote desert islands.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin showcases a collection of interesting and previously unseen finds from the show's travels round the country. The team visit St Albans Cathedral, Wolverhampton Art Gallery, the Platform in Morecambe and Grimsby Minster. The antiques experts are James Lewis, Clare Rawle, Christina Trevanion, Caroline Hawley, Michael Baggott and Charles Hanson. Paul also visits Packwood House in Warwickshire.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Harry Aikines-Aryeetey, Ania Magliano, Joe Swash and Jasmine Takhar take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo scales the Swiss Alps on one of the steepest cog railways in the world and marvels at the Pilatus Railway’s unique track design, which defies an astonishing 48 per cent maximum gradient. Michael overnights at the fairy-tale Grand Hotel Giessbach and learns how the beautiful 19th-century hotel was saved for and by the Swiss people. In Rotkreuz, a centre for cutting-edge healthcare and medical technology, he visits one of the world’s largest biotech companies. Michael’s final stop on this leg of his journey finds him at the Swiss Woodcarving Museum, where he chisels the cheeks of a king.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 1 highlights from the third Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: In Eastbourne, a routine day at the station changes in an instant when a boat catches fire just outside the harbour. In Trevone, north Cornwall, 18-year-old lifeguard Alfie races to the rescue of a surfer caught in a notorious rip current. On the Northumberland coast, the Blyth crew face a frantic search for a dog that’s been swept out by the tide. And in Burnham-in-Sea, in Somerset, reports of the crash landing of a hot air balloon lead the crew to launch on red alert.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as Curacao play Ivory Coast in their final Group E match at Philadelphia Stadium. Curacao is the smallest nation by both area and population to ever qualify for the World Cup. This is their debut appearance after first entering qualifying as an autonomous nation for the 2014 edition of the tournament. Ivory Coast are back after missing out on the previous two tournaments. They failed to get out of the group stage at their last three World Cups in 2006, 2010 and 2014. Manchester United’s Amad Diallo is a key player.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the final match in Group F, where Tunisia face Netherlands in Kansas City. The pride males turn against each other, an inexperienced mum puts her newborn cubs in mortal danger, a rival group of lions challenges the pride for its territory and, when lightning strikes, fires burn day and night. When the dust eventually settles, the pride is left with only one choice - to face their old foe, the elephants, or risk starvation. The final showdown awaits.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as South Africa play their final Group A game against South Korea in Monterrey. South Africa last played at a World Cup as the host nation in 2010, and they’re yet to make it past the group stage in three previous attempts. It's been 24 years since South Korea reached the semi-finals on home soil in 2002. They’ve made it to the round of 16 on two occasions since, including Qatar 2022, where they claimed a dramatic last-gasp win over Portugal in their final group game.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: The competition kicks off in Belfast as Vernon Kay and unreliable tour guide Paul Gorton serve up facts, fibs and playful distractions as the celebrity players attempt to sort truth from twaddle. This week’s guests are presenter Owain Wyn Evans, Olympic champion Greg Rutherford and Blue Peter’s Abby Cook, and their competition kicks off in Belfast. A daily winner is declared at the end of each show, with scores building across the five days as the race to reveal the week's overall champion gets going.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: On patrol in Belfast, Perri and Adam respond to reports of cars performing dangerous stunts on the streets while large crowds look on. When they arrive, the cars scatter and the Peelers don’t catch anyone. Later, they put in place an operation to disrupt a group of so-called differs – drivers who dangerously and illegally spin their cars in circles on main roads. The Peelers call in air support and try to catch a differ in the act. Back in Belfast, the team receive reports of two women being disruptive at a hotel. On arrival, one of the women greets Stephen and it looks like she’ll cooperate with police. But outside, things turn ugly, and after assaulting another woman, she is arrested and brought into custody. It’s not a quiet journey.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Richie Anderson is in rural Lincolnshire, helping John and Margaret find a large countryside home, with enough room for six visiting grandchildren, on a budget of £400,000. They explore wonderful properties, including one with a delightful garden, as well as a mystery house close to the coast. Richie also visits a former 300-acre farm now being transformed through an ambitious rewilding project.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: It's carnival time, one of the biggest celebrations of the summer season in Hamilton. Community Officer PC Chris Douglas is preparing for the island’s annual parade, swapping uniform for a handmade, colourful costume, while his colleagues stay on duty to keep the celebrations running smoothly as thousands line the streets to dance and party. Acting Inspector Tiffany Caisey and Sergeant Mervin Homer move from roadside stops to an unusual call at Dockyard, where a missing phone leads them to a cruise ship packed with 3,000 passengers and the tricky task of locating it on board. In central Hamilton, Sergeant Helen McHugh, K9 handler PC Robin MacNab and her dog Roni head into a park linked to drug activity tracking down a man, who when searched, reveals he’s in possession of a crack pipe and associated drug paraphernalia. Coastguard Corporal Quentin Burgess and Private Matthew Stephens are patrolling the waters, carrying out checks ahead of a busy maritime weekend. In the the run-up to carnival, Officer Chris teams up with PC Krishna Singh and PC Oba Swan to offer crime prevention advice to locals, a reminder of the close community ties that shape island life.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: A special programme from Birmingham in the heart of Gardeners’ World Live – an annual vibrant celebration of practical gardening and bold design. Monty Don is joined by Frances Tophill, Adam Frost, Arit Anderson and Sue Kent for an hour packed with ideas, inspiration and expert advice. The team explore standout gardens, meet the people shaping the future of horticulture and reveal practical takeaways viewers can try at home. Sustainability is in the spotlight as pioneering growers reveal why cork could be a game-changing material – and how it’s already transforming the way they garden. There’s a surprising and ambitious show garden co-designed by Professor Alice Roberts, bringing the story of evolution to life through plants, and a first-time designer whose passion for railways has inspired a unique garden guaranteed to turn heads.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The quiz show where players must avoid Impossible answers to stay in the competition. 21 people start today’s show but how many of them will survive to face the £10,000 question?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: In the final heat, four contenders take on the famous black chair, answering questions on their chosen specialist subjects to earn a place in the semi-finals. Clive Myrie hosts, with contenders answering questions on Christiaan Huygens, Jonathan Creek, the life and works of Artemisia Gentileschi, and European mammals.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Chris and Meg's Wild Summer
programme.desc: Chris Packham and stepdaughter Meg McCubbin visit a kittiwake colony, snorkel with grey seals, explore Lindisfarne island and take a boat to Bass Rock, home to 150,000 gannets.

programme.title: Britain and the Sea
programme.desc: This third episode traces the crucial importance of the sea to Britain's trade and to individual livelihoods of coastal communities. Joined on this leg of his epic sail by his son Fred, David follows the trade routes of the west coast of Scotland along the monumental channels that cut through the romantic Highlands and brought wealth and prosperity to the heart of Scotland. The journey starts at Craobh Haven and takes David along the Crinan Canal, around the Isle of Bute and up the River Clyde towards Glasgow.

programme.title: Wild West - America's Great Frontier
programme.desc: From the mysterious Sea of Cortez to the wild and elemental Pacific Ocean, powerful earth forces shape the coastline of the wild west. These restless shores are a magnet for life. They are visited by the greatest of all animals, the blue whale, and by strange fish that come ashore on the full moon to spawn in their thousands. Fog-shrouded headlands nurture massive coastal redwoods, and swollen-nosed lizards eke out a living on remote desert islands.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin showcases a collection of interesting and previously unseen finds from the show's travels round the country. The team visit St Albans Cathedral, Wolverhampton Art Gallery, the Platform in Morecambe and Grimsby Minster. The antiques experts are James Lewis, Clare Rawle, Christina Trevanion, Caroline Hawley, Michael Baggott and Charles Hanson. Paul also visits Packwood House in Warwickshire.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Harry Aikines-Aryeetey, Ania Magliano, Joe Swash and Jasmine Takhar take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo scales the Swiss Alps on one of the steepest cog railways in the world and marvels at the Pilatus Railway’s unique track design, which defies an astonishing 48 per cent maximum gradient. Michael overnights at the fairy-tale Grand Hotel Giessbach and learns how the beautiful 19th-century hotel was saved for and by the Swiss people. In Rotkreuz, a centre for cutting-edge healthcare and medical technology, he visits one of the world’s largest biotech companies. Michael’s final stop on this leg of his journey finds him at the Swiss Woodcarving Museum, where he chisels the cheeks of a king.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 1 highlights from the third Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: In Eastbourne, a routine day at the station changes in an instant when a boat catches fire just outside the harbour. In Trevone, north Cornwall, 18-year-old lifeguard Alfie races to the rescue of a surfer caught in a notorious rip current. On the Northumberland coast, the Blyth crew face a frantic search for a dog that’s been swept out by the tide. And in Burnham-in-Sea, in Somerset, reports of the crash landing of a hot air balloon lead the crew to launch on red alert.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as Curacao play Ivory Coast in their final Group E match at Philadelphia Stadium. Curacao is the smallest nation by both area and population to ever qualify for the World Cup. This is their debut appearance after first entering qualifying as an autonomous nation for the 2014 edition of the tournament. Ivory Coast are back after missing out on the previous two tournaments. They failed to get out of the group stage at their last three World Cups in 2006, 2010 and 2014. Manchester United’s Amad Diallo is a key player.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the final match in Group F, where Tunisia face Netherlands in Kansas City. Tunisia are at their seventh World Cup finals – their third in a row – but are yet to make it past the group stage despite beating France four years ago.

programme.desc: Ginger and the Pea-Rexes seek help from Watermelonsuchus to plug an underwater air vent.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: The Colourblocks decorate Purple's garden and learn about patterns. Discover how to make your own patterns.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Maisie finds out all about some very busy creatures – honeybees. Chantelle meets some of CBBC’s Show Me the Honey team, Darcey Mae and Curtis, as they show her inside a hive. While Rory and his son Sandy get an unusual view of a busy hive. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files explain how long honeybees live for, why they sting and whether they can smell flowers. It’s also time to find out how honeybees help the planet, and how the pollinators build a honeycomb. Sandy’s friend Zoe joins for this episode’s Teeny Tiny Task: making a wildflower seed ball.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Eden and Ava enjoy a family training session led by Dad who has lots of exercises for them! Can they complete 20 jumping jacks and who will win the relay race? Later, there’s a different kind of training as Eden and Ava meet up with their Uncle Leonard and his puppy Sky! Uncle Leonard shows them how to train a young dog. But will Sky listen to Eden’s commands? ... Sit!

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Preschool series celebrating foods from a rich diversity of backgrounds. Larry's family come from China. China is famous for its wonderful food, so Larry's friends are very excited to come over for his Chinese-themed meal. Larry's steamed tofu, egg and prawn recipe is cooked in his mum's special steamer but it can be made in an ordinary oven too. Larry's mum has even made some vegetable fried rice to serve with his dish. His friends try tofu for the first time and their reactions are very mixed. Let's see if they like tofu when it's cooked and eaten with the rest of the food. Larry even teaches them how to eat with chopsticks and they have lots of fun learning!

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Today, Maddie is finding out how clocks tell the time. She heads to a clock factory and uses a special time-lapse camera to show how the hands on the clock move around. Maddie also looks inside a battery-powered clock to see how they work. We see the tiny cogs that turn each of the hands so we can tell the time. Next, it's dinner time and Maddie visits a cutlery workshop to see how sheets of metal are made into forks. With a special microscope camera, we find out how the patterns are made using a special machine.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Tinks is a disability assistance dog for her owner, Charli, who has a condition that makes it painful for her to pick things up or to push and pull things. Tinks uses her superfetch skills to help Charli every day. The smallest of the Dog Squad gang, Tinks is a little Lhasa Apso with lots of big dog energy. Tinks and Charli are planting some seeds at the allotments. Tinks chats to her gardening friends the gnomes and braves the big dark shed to find Charli’s gardening gloves, before choosing some sunflower seeds and helping Charli to plant them. But when Charli sends Tinks on a mission to find the watering can, it turns out to be empty. The allotments are a big place for a little dog. Can Tinks find someone to help her and Charli water their seeds? Just wait until the rest of Dog Squad hear about their sunflower adventure!

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet an amazing snow leopard, a rare sight in the wild. They are called the ghosts of the mountains because you could live there your whole life and never see one. But Aneeshwar and Lizzie take viewers along to see one close up. Next, they meet a herd of yaks. These super furry animals have long, shaggy coats that keep them warm. Their coat is so thick, it’s like being wrapped up in 40 sleeping bags. Snow leopards and yaks are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: It's the day after the Brooklyn-Bells' wedding and time to say goodbye to the puppy. Evie goes with Jess to her veterinary practice to scan Waffle's microchip.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona turns bird detective and learns all about seagull behaviour.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of potatoes who sing songs in different genres. In this upbeat hip-hop song, the Small Potatoes introduce themselves and sing about their unique personalities.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Toad needs a new pumpkin double bass. Yukee and Twinkle use vegetables from the veggie patch to create some surprising instruments – but none are quite right for Toad. Can some new pumpkins be found, or will Toad be leaving music behind forever?

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Triggs is feeling a bit blue and finds it hard to get out of bed. That pesky birdie outside his window isn't helping either. But Maddie thinks she knows what the Birdie might be singing about and helps her friend step outside to greet the day.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee and the Squirrels have an exciting woodland adventure ahead of them, and everyone has their own routine to prepare for the day. Some are more keen on early starts than others – Happy is ready before his alarm, whereas Roly sleeps right through it. Whilst the Squirrels fuel up with important breakfasts, Roly’s family are still trying to wake him up. And only the promise of breakfast will do the trick! After freshening up, brushing their teeth and picking out the perfect outfit, the Squirrels start packing the essentials for their walk. They gawk at the amazing sights and interesting characters that they meet along the way, and they even get a magical lift home. It was well worth getting ready for that morning!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Are you sitting comfortably? Then we'll begin a bedtime story all about Numberblocks Six to Ten. Learn all about the numbers 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. U gets the balloon ride of his life, but he is still unhappy - or so he thinks! When unhappy U meets perky P, things can only go one way - up. Now U's only problem is getting back down. This episode introduces the letter U and the words up, cup, pup, pop, sum, mug and mud.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Ben meets Maliah and Betsy at the park, where they have fun in the playground and listen for sounds that are loud and quiet. Grandad Tumble is having a nap, and Mr Tumble tries not to make too much noise. There's musical fun in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words playground, grass and loud.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po receive a call on the Tubby Phone. It's the Tiddlytubbies, ringing to say hello just before the Tubby Phone Dance.

programme.title: Andy's Dinosaur Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back 150 million years to the time of brachiosaurus - a huge plant-eating dinosaur measuring 26 metres from nose to tail. His mission is to find a branch of a monkey puzzle tree - the favourite food of a brachiosaurus. But they are over 40 metres tall with no low branches - will Andy get his hands on one? And if he does, will he make it back to the museum in time before it opens?

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s Stall. She chooses the toy rabbit and remembers the day she got it. Daisy is meeting Suki in the Wobbly Coffee Pot today. Suki’s mum has said she’s allowed her first pet, and Daisy is going to help her decide on the perfect animal. Daisy thinks back to when she first got Little Mo, she felt so lucky. Unfortunately, Suki’s mum is allergic to cats and dogs, so a puppy isn’t a good idea. Suki remembers the time they found out Moira was allergic too, when she and Molly found a stray cat and kittens in the Big Hub. It made Moira very sneezy. They also remember when Mack brought Twinkle the pony to the Hub and left a big mess. But not as big a mess as the pigs at the farm. Suki thinks back to the time she and Daisy went to the farm and Willow the goat caused all sorts of bother. Maybe she should think about a smaller pet. Later, when Suki sees Mack unpacking a box of toy animals for his stall, it gives her a brilliant idea, and she finally thinks of the perfect pet.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: CBeebies’ very own motorcycle rider, Grace, show off three amazing machines that are made to help animals! First, Grace transports two horses in a horsebox, and then she shows off a boat made to study life under the ice caps. Finally, she drives a mobile animal operating theatre!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Eden and Ava pretend to cook some delicious food. Anyone for strawberry stew?

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: When a termite colony gets sucked into an aardvark’s nose, the Octos head to the rescue.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are helping Duggee clean his things, such as an old desk and lamp. They learn about stories which told that the lamp could grant three magical wishes. When they rub the lamp clean, they meet Professor Jeanie, who can grant them three wishes through the magic power of science. She amazes the Squirrels with her scientific experiments that bring their wishes alive, whilst educating them along the way. But before they wave goodbye, the Squirrels wonder if they can return the favour and grant a wish back to Professor Jeanie.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Fergie gets hiccups right before singing with her band, she calls on Vida for a quick preshow cure. None of Vida’s tricks work, but she knows what will - Fergie needs to get scared. And, luckily for Fergie, she gets stage fright!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: There are odd noises in the supermarket. Supertato discovers that Evil Pea and the Mini Peas are asleep and walking through the supermarket. Supertato tries to get them back to bed.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The Ducklings are building a train set and start bickering over who has the best idea. Weasy steps in to help, but his methods soon make things worse.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: How hard can it be to pick one plant at the top of a mountain with Mojo’s chopper top? Pretty hard when there’s a hungry goat who wants that plant even more than they do!

programme.desc: Nana reads an old story that Bandit wrote when he was five.

programme.desc: Mum and the kids set up a backyard obstacle course just for fun, but Dad wants to race!

programme.title: Zog

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: It’s the Den’s summer fete, and Jaz is excited to do a chicken and egg mascot dance with her dad, but soon realises she’s double-booked herself and might not have time to do both.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wants to blow a bubble just like her dads, but no matter how hard she tries, it won’t work. She makes a wish and creates a huge, magical bubble that floats around the park. As Rafi chases after it, the bubble spreads wonder wherever it goes. But when the bubble finally pops, Rafi is heartbroken. With help from her dads and friends, Rafi realises that bubbles aren’t meant to last forever, and that some of the most special moments are wonderful because they are fleeting.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: When JoJo runs out of storybooks to read at Gran Gran's house, she visits the library with Gran Gran and gets her very own card from Terrence the Librarian. JoJo learns all about the library and how it works, and discovers just how amazing it is; she is stuck for choice. JoJo feels very lucky to have a card that means she can borrow books to read over-and-over again.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. When Sarah hears some interesting music on the radio, she and Duck try and recreate it.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Tiny, Small, the Froglets and Baby Dragon are having great fun playing games with the Cloud. But when Major calls them all in for bed, the Cloud is left alone and sad. A little bit later Tiny discovers she has left something where they were playing and goes back up to get it. Finding a sad Cloud, she agrees to one last game - a magical flight up into space.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa create a leaf picture, but the wind blows the leaves away. At Play Time, they decorate a pot - but it breaks when BaBa accidentally drops it. At Yummy Time, they decorate a special cookie and bring it with them across the Lullaby Lake. They have been trying to make a gift for Gramma Leeba, who reassures them that the best gift is made with love.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: Series for young children about a magical place inhabited by a community of toy characters that care for each other and have fun together. Upsy Daisy sets up her own special megaphone to sing. Unfortunately, there is so much noise coming from the Tombliboos' house that she cannot make herself heard. Finally, all is well when everyone sings together.

programme.desc: Louis Theroux tells the story of Peggy, the pigeon who can't stop saying sorry.

programme.title: Bing

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies do conga dances over the hills, then they conga into Home Dome to answer the Tubby Phone and do a special conga Tubby Phone Dance. In Tummy Tales, the children have lots of fun as they conga around a soft play centre.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Explore the amazing world around us with baby monkey Tee and his Mum, Mo. Sing along, join in with stories and get ready for some family fun!

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Red is surprised to discover that she's not the only colour in the world when she meets Blue. Join the Colourblocks to learn which objects can be red and which can be blue, and how some can be both red and blue.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Pando is teaching Bing and Sula how to do little kicks and big kicks with a ball in the garden. Sula does the biggest kick of them all, but Bing kicks the ball the wrong way. As he tries to kick it back to Pando it bounces off the shed, breaking Flop's window! They have to stand statue-still while Flop cleans up the glass.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: There’s a girder out of place on Swoppiton Bridge, and unless Nori can fix it, that bridge is coming down! Luckily, Mojo’s got the tops, and Bo’s got the skills to help get it done.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Today, Worm and Ladybird welcome everyone to Squirrel Club. The Squirrels are wondering, what's that sound? It’s like Hey Duggee with ducks - Hey Quacky! Happy tells his chums about getting his first pair of glasses when he was little. Of course, the other Squirrels have questions.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Out for a walk, the Squirrels spot an interesting poster - it’s King Tiger advertising his Roar Talent Show. Naturally, the Squirrels are very keen to take part. First, they need to find their talents. After they spend some time searching, Narrator explains that ‘finding their talents’ means working out what they are good at. So, the Squirrels practise their skills until they are ready to face an audience.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Mum and the kids set up a backyard obstacle course just for fun, but Dad wants to race!

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Cotton-tail's birthday cake is stolen and Peter vows to get it back, he finds himself in hot water with a host of angry villains!

programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. When Kwazii gets lost at sea aboard the tiny Octo-Ski, he meets a flotilla of even tinier sea skaters - the only insects who live on the ocean.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Learn how much fun counting can be with the Numberblocks - a fun-loving group of numbers who work together to solve problems big and small.

programme.desc: After a spate of unfortunate accidents, Pancake is convinced that rubbing a lucky icicle will bring him good luck but panics when it’s rubbed away, until his friends step in.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella and Lift visit the Sing Song Forest, where Tincy the Spider needs help from the Playtimers to wake up her furry friend, Hedge the Hedgehog.

programme.title: Bing

programme.title: Yakka Dee!

The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch

programme.desc: Kiri sings a song about how wonderful it is to have your very own body.

The Twirlywoos eventually catch up with the small butterfly when the Hooter calls them home and they lift off into the air, and they find themselves flying beside it. Back on the boat, the Twirlywoos are tickled by a little starfish which comes out of Peekaboo's house. To avoid being caught, the starfish keeps on shrinking, getting smaller and smaller until it gets so tiny that it disappears altogether!
